# Daily Macro Digest — 4 August 2026

## Summary
The big story is oil's sharp reversal: WTI and Brent both dropped hard (-5.5% and -7.3%) after headlines pointed to a de-escalation in the Iran conflict ("Trump's Iran Reversal Sends European Gas Prices Tumbling"), unwinding some of the Middle East supply-risk premium that had been supporting crude. US 10Y yields fell alongside (-1.24%), while gold and silver drifted higher (+1.5%, +1.3%) despite that being a fairly muted, non-anomalous move for both. The US dollar index ticked up slightly, AUD/USD eased marginally, VIX stayed subdued, and ASX materials were roughly flat-to-soft (-0.94%) — nothing here suggests a broad risk-off day, just an oil-specific unwind.

## Flagged Assets

**WTI Crude (-5.5%, anomaly)**
Sharp drop coinciding with headlines on a partial Iran conflict de-escalation, reversing part of the Hormuz-related supply-risk premium (relationship #1 working in reverse). Historical context: only 1 prior similar episode recorded (27 Jul, -8.2%), too small a sample to draw a pattern — in that single case, oil was volatile in the days after, swinging both down and sharply up.

**Brent Crude (-7.3%, anomaly)**
Same driver as WTI, more pronounced. With 3 prior similar down-move episodes recorded, the pattern is mixed: cumulative moves over the following days ranged from -9.8% to +5.6% depending on the episode — not a reliable directional signal, just evidence that big down-days in Brent have historically been followed by more volatility, not a clean continuation either way.

**US 10Y Yield (-1.24%, anomaly)**
Yields fell alongside the oil move — plausibly reflecting reduced inflation-risk premium as the geopolitical supply threat eased (opposite side of relationship #1). Only 1 prior episode on record, so no reliable pattern; that single instance saw yields drift modestly higher over the following days.

**Gold & Silver (not flagged, but notable)**
Both rose ~1.3-1.5% even as oil fell and the safe-haven trigger (Hormuz tension) eased — a bit contrary to relationship #1's usual gold-oil linkage. VIX was flat and the dollar firmed slightly, so this doesn't read as classic risk-off buying; more likely just noise given the moves aren't statistically unusual for either metal.

## What to Watch
- Further developments on the Iran/US conflict status — headlines still flag unresolved tension (Bab el-Mandeb tanker activity, "Why the US Can't Easily Exit the Iran Conflict"), so the oil de-escalation narrative could reverse.
- Any confirmation or follow-through on the reported Iran deal — determines whether oil's drop holds or partially retraces.
- Watch AUD/USD and ASX materials for any China demand data this week (not present in today's headlines, but relevant per relationship #4).

*This is informational context only, not trading advice.*
